scope.note: This repository holds NO repository-level secrets. Every credential below is environment-scoped, which is why each new environment forces fresh hand-provisioning and why P-6 precondition reachability is the governing question for all of them. Measured 2026-08-07 with `gh secret list --repo rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev` (empty) and `gh api repos/rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev/environments`.

expiry.reason: A raw ed25519 private key carries no expiry of its own. Its AUTHORITY expires: each issued attestation has a 24-hour lifetime, and the key is only as current as the trust root pinned in the frozen bundle.

reestablishing_transition.detail: This key reached this environment by a manual out-of-band act. No registered transition re-establishes it. Rotating it would need FRESH key material, and Rex's binding ruling forbids any walkthrough that asks the owner to generate, paste, or hold a signing key value, so the correct fix is an in-platform key-generation-and-rotation transition that does not yet exist.

compensating_lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The key is exercised on every renewal. If it were lost or corrupted, the very next scheduled renewal fails at the signing step, at least 6 hours before the live 24-hour authority could expire. Detection therefore precedes outage rather than following it.
compensating_lapse_detection.residual_risk: Detection is not prevention. If the key is LOST there is no registered path to restore it; the system would fail closed and stay closed until the missing rotation transition is built.

expiry.reason: Same key material as the issuer-held copy; no credential-level expiry.

reestablishing_transition.invocation: gh workflow run provision-renewal-signing-key.yml --repo rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev --ref main -f mode=copy
reestablishing_transition.detail: Reads the key from rea-write-enforcement-issuer and writes it to rea-write-enforcement-renewal through the GitHub secrets API public-key encryption path. Idempotent; verifies the target secret by name and refuses unless the observed updated_at proves THIS run wrote it.
owner_acts: approve the one rea-write-enforcement-issuer deployment this workflow requests

expiry.reason: Not yet minted. GitHub fixes a fine-grained PAT's expiry at mint time and the owner chooses it, so the real date IS knowable and MUST be written into this row at provisioning. Recording it is part of the provisioning step, not an afterthought.

lapse_detection.cadence: on demand, and as the first action of any mode=copy run
lapse_detection.how_it_detects: probe_write_scope() GETs the target environment's secrets public-key endpoint before writing anything. An expired or revoked PAT fails that probe and produces the typed refusal SECRETS_WRITE_PAT_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE naming the exact permission required, instead of a partial write.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: The probe fires only when the workflow is invoked. A PAT that lapses between invocations is discovered at the next invocation, which is acceptable because nothing depends on the PAT between invocations.

reestablishing_transition.sanctioned_by: Rex ruling 2026-08-07 (Option A, binding): the owner's only acts are to mint a PAT and to approve one issuance.
owner_acts: mint a fine-grained PAT scoped to repository rexcoleman/rexcoleman.dev only, permission Secrets: Read and write
store it as environment secret REA_SECRETS_WRITE_PAT in rea-write-enforcement-issuer
record its expiry date in this file
reestablishing_transition.detail: This is the bootstrap root of the custody chain. It is a manual act by construction: a token that lets automation write secrets cannot itself be established by automation that has no secrets. It is recorded as a sanctioned owner act rather than hidden, and it never involves key material -- the owner mints a token, never a signing key.

expiry.reason: GitHub App private keys do not expire. They are valid until explicitly revoked in the App's settings.

reestablishing_transition.detail: Re-establishment requires generating a new private key in the GitHub App settings UI and hand-provisioning it. No registered transition exists, and none can read the key out of App settings, so this is structurally the same class of gap as the issuer signing key.

compensating_lapse_detection.cadence: every independent second-principal review, i.e. every capability_change issuance
compensating_lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The key is consumed by actions/create-github-app-token at the start of the review job. A revoked key fails token minting immediately and blocks the review rather than producing an unattested pass.
compensating_lapse_detection.residual_risk: Only exercised on capability_change issuances, so a revocation could sit undetected between them. It cannot cause a silent WRONG result -- it fails closed -- but it can surface late.

expiry.reason: `gh secret list` and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{env}/secrets return created_at and updated_at ONLY. GitHub exposes no expiry field for a secret's CONTENTS, and the contents are write-only, so no automated path in this repository can read or derive this token's expiry. The date is not being withheld; it is genuinely unavailable. Do not fabricate one.

lapse_detection.detector: .github/workflows/renew-write-enforcement-attestation.yml -> issue-write-enforcement-attestation.yml job renew-wea, step 'Checkout frozen repositories'
lapse_detection.how_it_detects: This is the structural compensation for an unreadable expiry. The token is exercised by checkout_manifest.py on every renewal attempt. A lapsed token fails that step, and because renewal runs 4 times inside each 24-hour authority lifetime, the failure is observed at least 6 hours BEFORE the live attestation expires. Lapse therefore surfaces as a failed run while enforcement is still valid, which is exactly the window in which it can be fixed without an outage. Silent lapse -- the failure mode that already cost this cycle an outage -- is what this structure removes.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: Surfacing depends on someone seeing the failed run. The run failure itself is deterministic and unmissable in the Actions list, but proactive alerting on it has NOT been independently verified and is a separate open item.

reestablishing_transition.sanctioned_by: Rex ruling 2026-08-07 (Option A, binding): minting a token is a sanctioned owner act; only signing-key material is forbidden.
owner_acts: mint a read-scoped token over the frozen bundle member repositories
store it as environment secret REA_BUNDLE_READ_TOKEN in rea-write-enforcement-issuer
record the mint date and chosen expiry in this file
reestablishing_transition.detail: Once REA_SECRETS_WRITE_PAT exists this becomes mechanizable the same way the renewal signing key was, but that is a distinct transition and is deliberately not claimed here before it is built.

expiry.reason: Same as REA_BUNDLE_READ_TOKEN: the GitHub secrets API exposes created_at and updated_at only, never an expiry for the secret's contents.

lapse_detection.how_it_detects: The token is exercised by `gh api repos/rexcoleman/newsletter/rulesets/19564990` on every renewal attempt, and the following step refuses a ruleset response that does not normalize. A lapsed token fails at least 6 hours before the live authority expires.
lapse_detection.residual_risk: Same as REA_BUNDLE_READ_TOKEN: detection is deterministic, proactive alerting is unverified.

store it as environment secret REA_RULESET_READ_TOKEN in rea-write-enforcement-issuer
